title: Cuando era pequeña
blurbEn: The third past tense, and the friendliest: only three irregular verbs in the whole language. It is for how things used to be.
body:
Cuando era pequeña, vivía en un pueblo muy pequeño con mis padres y mi hermana.

Todos los días iba al colegio a pie. El colegio estaba cerca de casa y el camino era muy tranquilo, entre árboles y campos.

Por las tardes jugaba en la plaza con mis amigos hasta la hora de cenar. Nadie nos vigilaba y nadie tenía miedo.

En verano nadábamos en el río y volvíamos a casa con hambre.

Mi abuela vivía con nosotros y cocinaba todos los domingos. La casa olía muy bien.

Éramos felices y no lo sabíamos. Ahora lo recuerdo todo con mucho cariño.
translationEn:
When I was small, I lived in a very small village with my parents and my sister.

Every day I went to school on foot. The school was near home and the way there was very peaceful, between trees and fields.

In the afternoons I played in the square with my friends until dinner time. Nobody watched over us and nobody was afraid.

In summer we swam in the river and came home hungry.

My grandmother lived with us and cooked every Sunday. The house smelled wonderful.

We were happy and we did not know it. Now I remember it all very fondly.

era.note: Imperfecto of 'ser'. One of only three irregular verbs in this whole tense.

iba.note: Imperfecto of 'ir'. Note it does not look like 'fui' at all — different tense, different stem.

vivía.note: Regular: -er and -ir verbs take -ía. No exceptions worth worrying about.

phrases.note: The classic opening for childhood memories, and the reason this unit is named after it.
A repeated habit, not a single event. That is what this tense is for.
